title: Body Surface Area (Chemo BSA)
desc: Body surface area in m² from body weight, with common mg/m² doses converted to milligrams for the patient in front of you. Clinician reference.

meds.name: Common mg/m² doses converted
meds.desc: the amount to give at each per-m² dose
meds.note: Multiply any per-m² dose by the BSA above. The sheet also cross-checks 0.02 mg/kg against 0.5 mg/m² — for a typical dog these land close together, but they diverge sharply at the extremes of size, which is the whole reason BSA is used for cytotoxics.

notes.Formula: BSA (m²) = 0.101 × body weight in kg raised to the power 2/3. This is the standard canine conversion, and the one the source spreadsheet uses.
notes.Why BSA and not mg/kg: Cytotoxic drugs are dosed per square metre because surface area tracks metabolic rate better than weight does. Dosing a very small dog by mg/kg overdoses it relative to a large one.
notes.Worked check: A 22.5 kg dog has a BSA of 0.806 m². A 2.27 kg dog (5 lb) has a BSA of 0.175 m².
notes.Small patients: Below about 10 kg, BSA-based dosing of cytotoxics can overdose the patient. Many protocols switch to mg/kg under that threshold — check the specific protocol before relying on the per-m² figure.
notes.Handling: Cytotoxic drugs need cytotoxic handling — closed systems, gloves, and appropriate disposal of waste and patient excreta.
